description: Reads one thread whole: every message in order with its direction, its language and its attachments, the contact fiche, the mailbox the thread arrived through, the draft awaiting review when there is one, and in "notes" what the team left on the thread for each other, oldest first, with who wrote each one. Notes are never part of "messages" and were never sent to anyone. A message the mailbox sent carries "delivery" when the mail system tracked it: per recipient (Bcc included), "state" is "delivered" (accepted by the recipient's server, which says nothing of the inbox or of reading), "deferred" (retried by itself for five days), "bounced", "returned" (accepted, then a non-delivery report came back) or "expired", with the server's own "remote_reply" and a "reason" in plain words. When the thread was filed as it arrived, "filed_reason" says why: "spam_filter" for the filter's verdict, "blocked_sender" for a sender the account had reported, and "spoofed_own_domain" for a mail showing one of the account's own domains whose DMARC check failed, which lands in Spam in a mailbox (mark_not_spam takes it back out) and, on a helpdesk queue, in the Trash with its ticket closed (file_conversation with "inbox" brings it back, open). Read this before writing an answer. To read several threads, give conversation_id the list of their ids, in ONE call rather than one call per thread: the answer then lists in "results" the outcome of each thread in the order given ("ok", with its "result" or its "error") and counts "succeeded" and "failed". Each thread passes exactly the checks it would alone, so one refused or out of reach ("not found") leaves the others done, and the call is an error only when none succeeded.

conversation_id.description: The id of the conversation, as list_conversations gives it, or a list of up to 20 ids to do the same to every one of them in a single call.

name: get_conversation
title: Read a conversation
